approved_repository_evidence: .ai-ops/evidence/PP-RELAY-036-benham-via-lascivia.md — Benham (The Laws of Scientific Hand Reading, 1900) recognizes the Via Lascivia as a sister line to the Mercury line, describes its slanting course from the inside/base of the Mount of Moon to the lower part of the upper Mount of Moon near the percussion, and gives its historical name's origin in an older reading linking surplus vitality/energy on a sensual hand type to lascivious behavior, explicitly qualified that a non-sensual hand could express the same energy in other activity instead. source_preflight.notes: Prevalence: the only frequency-adjacent claim found by audit:claim-risk ('the Mercury line often begins' near the Mount of Luna) was reworded to remove the frequency assertion, since the evidence note does not support it; the article otherwise makes no claim about how common the Via Lascivia itself is. Historical/scientific claims: every interpretive statement (course, sister-line relationship, historical name origin, non-sensual-hand qualification) is directly traceable to the evidence note's 'verified safe claim boundary'; the medical-exclusion section states plainly that the reviewed source does not address health/allergy at all, per the evidence note's 'important exclusions' list. Combination readings: the article explicitly declines to extend the Mercury line's own health/business associations to the Via Lascivia beyond what Benham himself states, and introduces no reading involving other lines, mounts, or hand type beyond the single surplus-energy/hand-type qualification the evidence note authorizes. Vague attribution: an initial draft phrase ('earlier palmists described') was reworded to 'Benham's text describes' to avoid unattributed authority language, since the older reading is Benham's own account of a prior tradition, not an independent appeal to unnamed sources; no 'modern palmists'/'some writers'/'experts' phrasing appears anywhere. Claim-type separation: location/course and historical-name sections are explicitly Benham-attributed; the 'allergy line' and medical-safety framing is explicit Palmistry Path editorial guidance, kept in its own section and FAQ entries, visibly distinct from the historical material. Quotation fidelity: no quotation marks are used around any Benham content; a draft phrase quoting an untranslated Latin gloss was reworded to remove the quotation marks since the exact translation wording was not independently verified against Benham's edition, per the evidence note's paraphrase-only instruction; the Via Lascivia line name itself and the 'allergy line' search term are set in quotes only as the term/name being discussed, not as claimed Benham quotations. Safety boundaries: no medical, legal, financial, deterministic-relationship, criminality, or predictive-science claim is introduced; the article explicitly directs allergy/health questions to a qualified medical professional.
